title: Check the remote binary is owned by the user and not other-writable before exec
description:
Security, hardening a predictable exec path. ssh.rs prelude execs $HOME/.local/share/acs/<version>/acs whenever it is executable, and install.rs creates that directory with a bare mkdir -p under the remote umask. Nothing verifies the directory or the binary is owned by the user and not group- or other-writable.

On a host where $HOME or ~/.local/share is group-writable (umask 002 with a shared group, a common lab or edge-device setup) another local user plants a binary at that exact path and every later `acs <host>` execs it as the victim. It is the generic writable-home problem, but acs adds a predictable, always-exec'd path and never checks it.

Done when the prelude refuses a candidate whose directory or file is not owned by the user or is writable by group or other, falling back to the install path with a clear message, and a test covers a loosened directory.
close_reason: Implemented in #132: the prelude checks ownership and writability before exec

title: Emit a newline before the ACS-READY/ACS-NEED marker so printf noise cannot swallow it
description:
`parse_marker` (src/proto.rs ~L636) requires the marker to start a line. A `printf "foo"` (no `\n`) in a startup file makes the line `fooACS-READY 1` / `fooACS-NEED ...`, which is rejected. For ACS-NEED the client reports "the connection closed before acs started"; for ACS-READY the client blocks in `dial` waiting for a marker while the proxy blocks waiting for HELLO — a mutual hang with no timeout on either side (see the dial-deadline bead).

Done when `ready_line()` and the prelude's `printf` (src/ssh.rs) emit a leading `\n`, with a scanner test for noise without a trailing newline.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests (bugs-install branch)

title: Chmod the payload-path binary to 0755 explicitly instead of relying on the umask
description:
install::write_exe (src/install.rs:282-294) relies on OpenOptions::mode(0o755), which the remote umask masks (umask 077 gives 0700), whereas the self-copy path (install.rs:126) does an explicit chmod 755. Only matters if the per-user directory is ever shared, but the two paths disagree and tests/install.rs asserts 0755 only on the self-copy path.

Done when write_exe sets the mode after writing and the install test asserts 0755 on the payload path under a restrictive umask.
close_reason: Implemented in #95 (eeb5969)

title: Package acs for Homebrew with a tap updated on release
description:
Package acs for distribution with Homebrew.

User's ask: "package the application for distribution with Homebrew".

Today acs ships as GitHub release archives (acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz for macOS arm64/x86_64 and Linux x86_64/aarch64, plus SHA256SUMS), the one-line installer, and `acs upgrade` (docs/VERSIONING.md, scripts/release-binaries.sh).

Proposed shape:

- A tap repository, `michel-onstein/homebrew-acs`, with `Formula/acs.rb` that installs the prebuilt release archive for the machine (on_macos/on_linux, on_arm/on_intel), with its sha256 from SHA256SUMS. `brew install michel-onstein/acs/acs`. A prebuilt binary keeps the complete build with its Linux payloads (DESIGN §8.1); building from source would give a slim build that cannot install other platforms' remotes.
- The formula is updated by the release: scripts/release-binaries.sh (or `cargo xtask`) rewrites version, URLs and sha256s and pushes to the tap after publishing.
- `brew test`: `acs --version` reports the version.
- A Homebrew-installed acs should not replace itself: `acs upgrade` detects it runs from a Homebrew Cellar path and says `brew upgrade acs`, and the weekly update-check message suggests the same.
- README "Install" lists `brew install`.

Done when `brew install michel-onstein/acs/acs` installs the current release on macOS (and Linuxbrew), `brew test acs` passes, a release updates the formula automatically, and `acs upgrade` defers to brew for a brewed install.
close_reason: Implemented with tests: tap michel-onstein/homebrew-acs, formula rendered and pushed on release, acs upgrade defers to brew (PR #27)

title: Warn when the latest release reported is older than the last one seen
description:
Security, update freeze. upgrade::decide correctly refuses to install an older release unless --version pins it, so a straight rollback is blocked. But an attacker controlling the channel, or a stale mirror, can serve an old but genuine SHA256SUMS indefinitely: decide reports nothing to do, the weekly check stays silent, and the user sits on a vulnerable version with no signal. There is no freshness or expiry metadata.

update_check's State already persists the last latest it saw, so the comparison is nearly free.

Done when a reported latest older than the stored one produces a visible warning rather than silence, the stored value is not overwritten by the older one, and a test covers the regression.
close_reason: Implemented in #134: a channel offering an older release is reported once

title: Add a curl | sh installer for acs (per-platform install dir)
description:
Add a one-line installer: `curl -fsSL <url> | sh` installs acs the way the platform expects.

User's ask: "create an install script that someone can download which installs acs automatically according to the rules of the platform it is being installed on. Similar to other apps: `curl <something> | <some shell command>`."

Proposed design:

- `scripts/install.sh`, POSIX sh. It is also published as a release asset by `scripts/release-binaries.sh`, so the stable URL is `https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases/latest/download/install.sh`. The repo is public.
- It maps `uname -s` / `uname -m` to one of the four release targets: macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/aarch64. Anything else is a clear error.
- It downloads `acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` from the release (latest by default; `ACS_VERSION=0.2.0` pins one) and refuses to install on a checksum mismatch. It uses `curl` or `wget`, and `shasum -a 256` or `sha256sum`.
- Install location follows each platform's rules: per-user `~/.local/bin` (XDG) by default, or `/usr/local/bin` when run as root or with `ACS_INSTALL_DIR`. It warns, with the line to add, when the directory is not on `PATH`.
- Re-running it upgrades in place, and it prints the installed `acs --version`.

Today install is manual: README "Install" has a curl + tar + install recipe, and the release assets exist since v0.1.0.

Done when: the script passes shellcheck; tests run it against a real release in Alpine and Ubuntu containers and in a temp HOME on macOS (default dir, pinned version, checksum failure, unsupported platform); README leads with the one-liner.
close_reason: Implemented: scripts/install.sh (curl|sh, wget fallback, SHA256SUMS check, versioned layout ~/.local or /usr/local, ACS_VERSION/ACS_INSTALL_DIR), published as a release asset; scripts/test_install.sh passes on macOS, Alpine and Ubuntu as root and user

title: Verify the uploaded binary on the remote before executing it
description:
Security, self-attested integrity. The remote install script is `set -e; mkdir -p <dir>; cat > <tmp>; chmod 755 <tmp>; exec <tmp> _install --finish --token <t> --sha256 <digest>` (install.rs). Verified by reading it: the uploaded file is made executable and RUN, and the digest the client computed is then checked by the very binary being checked, which hashes its own current_exe(). A substituted binary simply skips the check and prints ok, which is all side_call looks for. In the payload path the appended blob is only structurally parsed by Payloads::parse and never checksummed.

Attack: anyone who can replace the file between the cat and the exec (a second person on a shared account, a compromised sshd, a remote whose $HOME is writable by others) gets their code run and then installed at ~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs, which every later acs connection execs.

Already good, so do not redo it: the token is 64 bits from /dev/urandom, write_exe uses create_new (O_EXCL), and parse_finish rejects a non-hex token.

Done when the client verifies the digest before the binary is executed (a shasum/sha256sum call on the remote, or reading the file back) and the payload blob is digested too, with a test that a tampered upload is refused.
close_reason: Implemented in #113: the remote shell checks the digest before the upload can run

title: Ping IPv6 alias hosts on macOS, where ping is IPv4-only
description:
alias::ping_with (src/alias.rs:237-252) runs the system ping and takes status.success() as reachable. macOS ping is IPv4-only: `ping -c 1 -t 2 -- ::1` exits 68 "cannot resolve", so an IPv6 literal or a name with only AAAA records can never be chosen.

Scenario: aliases: nas: [{host: "fd00:1::20"}] or an IPv6-only LAN name. With -v acs logs "does not answer ping within 500ms" every time and exits 255, or falls back to the wrong entry, although ssh would connect fine. prefer_local_network explicitly matches IPv6 networks (README, netmatch tests with fd00:1::5/64), so a user on an IPv6 LAN sees "is on the local network fd00:1::/64" followed by "does not answer ping". Linux iputils ping is dual-stack, so this is macOS-specific.

Done when an IPv6 literal (or a ping exit 68 on macOS) uses ping6, or the README documents reachability_check: false for such hosts, with a test for the IPv6 literal path.
close_reason: Implemented in #79 (1fea487)

title: Carry a half-read frame over the proxy's HELLO hand-off to the relay
description:
proxy::attach (src/proxy.rs:280-285) re-encodes only complete frames left in dec (`while let Ok(Some(m)) = dec.next_msg()`); bytes of an incomplete frame (dec.pending() > 0) are discarded, and relay_fds then reads fresh from stdin, forwarding the remainder of that frame to the master with its head missing. The master's decoder desyncs, answers BAD_REQUEST/Closing, and the client exits with code::ERROR.

Latent today: the client sends nothing between HELLO and WELCOME (stdin and SIGWINCH are gated on welcomed, client.rs:885-903). Any future pipelining after HELLO (e.g. sending the unacked resend with the HELLO) would hit it. Decoder::take_rest() exists for exactly this and pick.rs uses it.

Done when attach appends dec.take_rest() to the bytes forwarded to the master, with a proxy test that splits a RESIZE across the hand-off.
close_reason: Implemented in #97 (4996762)

title: Bound the key lexer string state so command mode cannot be suppressed
description:
Security, denial of the detach key. keys.rs enters Lex::Str on ESC ] , ESC P or ESC _ from stdin and then forwards every byte raw without calling token(), so Ctrl-] is not recognised, command mode cannot arm and Detach cannot fire. The only way out is the 100 ms idle timeout in tick, which never fires while bytes keep arriving.

Attack: a malicious remote sets a multi-megabyte clipboard with OSC 52 and queries it back in a loop. The terminal streams one enormous continuously-arriving reply, the user's Ctrl-] Ctrl-] d is swallowed into it and forwarded to the attacker instead, and the session cannot be detached without killing the terminal. DESIGN §6.3 documents the timeout as the mitigation for the Alt+_ case only; the adversarial case is not considered.

Related to the already-filed Alt+_ lexer bug, which is the accidental version of the same state.

Done when the string state is bounded by total bytes as well as idle time, the command key is recognised even inside it (or the state is abandoned on a cap), and a test streams an unending OSC reply and still detaches.
close_reason: Implemented in #121: the string state is bounded by bytes as well as by silence

title: Let a fork set at build time which repo updates come from
description:
User's words: "is it possible at release time to specify which github repo updates are coming from? This is needed in case someone wants to fork".

Today it is not. The update source can only be changed at **runtime, per environment**, never baked into the binary a fork ships.

Verified (v0.11.4):

- `release::DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL` (src/release.rs:16) is a plain hardcoded const, `https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases`.
- `release::releases_url()` (src/release.rs:35) lets `ACS_RELEASES_URL` override it, and that is honoured by `acs upgrade` (upgrade.rs:273) and the weekly update check (update_check.rs:220), and separately by scripts/install.sh:25-26. The guards from acs-95w stay as they are: https only unless `--allow-insecure-url` is passed on the command line, and ignored outright when the real and effective uid differ.
- There is no config-file setting for it: `local_networks` and friends are in `config::KEYS`, a releases URL is not.
- `build.rs` already emits `cargo:rustc-env=ACS_TARGET`, so the compile-time mechanism needed here is in place and used.

So a fork has two bad options: patch the const (a merge conflict on every upstream sync) or tell every one of its users to export `ACS_RELEASES_URL` forever.

Change: let the default be chosen at build time, falling back to today's constant.

```rust
// build.rs
println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL");
if let Ok(u) = std::env::var("ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL") {
    println!("cargo:rustc-env=ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL={u}");
}

// src/release.rs
pub const DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL: &str = match option_env!("ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL") {
    Some(u) => u,
    None => "https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases",
};
```

This is not a loosening of acs-95w. The runtime guards exist because the environment is attacker-controllable across a privilege boundary; a compiled-in value is chosen by whoever builds the binary, who already decides what it does. The sudo and https rules on the runtime override are untouched.

The other places a fork must still change, which this bead should cover or explicitly leave out:

| Where | What | Overridable today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| src/release.rs:16 | update check, `acs upgrade` | env only |
| src/install.rs:85 `INSTALLER` | the `curl ... \| sh` line in the "not installed" message (install.rs:96) | no, hardcoded |
| scripts/install.sh:25 | the installer's own default | `ACS_RELEASES_URL` |
| xtask/src/formula.rs:9 `REPO` | Homebrew formula URLs | no |
| xtask/src/package.rs:31,35 | install instructions written into NOTES.md | no |
| scripts/update-tap.sh:30 | which tap to push | `ACS_TAP_REPO` (already done) |

`update-tap.sh` already anticipated this; nothing else did. `INSTALLER` is only used in a message, so it is cosmetic, but it sends a fork's users upstream to install and should derive from the same base.

Interacts with acs-o9v (sign release artifacts), which is parked on a signing-scheme decision: if a fork publishes its own releases, the key embedded in the binary has to be the fork's key too. Whatever mechanism lands here for the URL is the natural one for the key, so o9v should be designed with this in mind rather than hardcoding one key. Not a blocking dependency in either direction — they are coupled by design, not by order.

Nothing in docs/ covers forking at all: a grep for "fork" over docs/ and README.md finds only `forkpty`.

Done when the default releases URL can be set at build time and falls back to today's value when unset, `INSTALLER` derives from the same base rather than being its own const, a test covers both the unset and the set case, and a short "Forking" section in docs/VERSIONING.md lists every knob a fork must set (the build-time URL, `ACS_TAP_REPO`, the xtask formula/package strings) so the list above does not have to be rediscovered.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #153 (be220ed): ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL at build time, installer() derives from it, Forking section in VERSIONING.md

title: acs v1: single-binary persistent ssh sessions
description:
Implement `acs` as designed in `docs/DESIGN.md`: one Rust binary that is the
local client, the per-connection remote proxy and the per-session remote
master, replacing the `dsh` shell function (ssh + dtach).

Invariants every child must preserve:

- Unfiltered stream: pty bytes reach the local terminal verbatim; keystrokes
  reach the pty verbatim except the command key (DESIGN §2, §6).
- Transport is the system `ssh`; no ssh-side configuration (DESIGN §3).
- Lossless resume after a network drop (DESIGN §5.2).

Done when every child is closed and DESIGN.md's Status reads Built.
close_reason: All 25 children closed: acs v1 implemented, tested on macOS and Linux, verified end to end over real ssh

title: Scaffold the acs crate: size-tuned profile, role dispatch, verify script
description:
Create the Cargo project the rest of the plan builds on (DESIGN §9).

- `Cargo.toml`: release profile `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`,

- `src/main.rs`: role dispatch — default client; hidden `_proxy`, `_master`,

- Module skeleton per DESIGN §9 layout (`proto.rs`, `client/`, `master/`,
  `proxy.rs`, `install.rs`) and an `xtask/` workspace member placeholder.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo test`, `npx markdownlint-cli2` on `**/*.md`.
- Flip DESIGN.md `Status:` to "In progress" and its CLAUDE.md index row, in
  the same change (repo convention).

Acceptance: `scripts/verify.sh` passes; `cargo zigbuild --release --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` build; the slim
binary size for each target is recorded in the PR/commit message as the
baseline against the < 1 MB budget.

title: Master: session protocol, takeover, resume, resize, kill
description:
The master's side of the protocol (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2, §5.3).

- HELLO handling with attach / create / attach-or-create; WELCOME with
  instance id and resumed / gap / fresh.
- One active client: a new attach sends TAKEOVER to the previous one.
- Output: pty reads go into the ring; DATA frames from the client's offset;
  backpressure while attached (stop reading the pty when unsent bytes would
  be overwritten); ring wraps freely while detached.
- Input: INPUT dedupe by seq, ACK.
- RESIZE via `TIOCSWINSZ`; on a fresh attach force a redraw by signalling
  `tcgetpgrp(pty)` with SIGWINCH even when the size is unchanged.
- PING/PONG; DETACH; KILL = SIGHUP to the child's process group, SIGKILL
  after 3 s; EXIT{status} to the client on child exit.

Tests (framed test client over the unix socket): resume from an offset
yields exactly the missed bytes; offset beyond the ring yields gap; a new
instance yields fresh; takeover; KILL kills a process group that ignores
SIGHUP; backpressure engages with a stalled client and not when detached.
close_reason: Master protocol verified by 10 integration tests: exact resume replay, gap and fresh attach, same-identity silent takeover vs BUSY + force, KILL SIGHUP then SIGKILL after 3s, backpressure for a stalled client and none while detached, resize, forced redraw on fresh attach, input dedupe

title: Proxy: connect-or-spawn master and relay frames
description:
`acs _proxy <session> <mode> --proto N` (DESIGN §3, §4.3).

- Resolve the socket directory; connect; on ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED unlink a
  stale socket and start the master (create modes only), waiting for its
  readiness report.
- Write `ACS-READY <proto>` to stdout before the first frame.
- Check the protocol version in the client's HELLO; on mismatch answer
  ERROR telling the user to finish or kill the session.
- Splice stdin/stdout <-> socket until either side closes.

Tests: stale socket replaced; two proxies racing to create converge on one
master; mismatched protocol version yields ERROR.
close_reason: proxy.rs: connect-or-start (retries when another master wins), ACS-READY, HELLO proto check, --new naming under dir lock, splice relay, --list; 7 integration tests via stdio incl. stale socket, racing proxies, mismatch, missing session, --new numbering, dropped client detaches

title: Session listing (--list) via STATUS
description:
`acs <host> --list` (DESIGN §4.3, §4.5).

- Master answers STATUS with name, attached/detached, attached identity (or
  last attached), creator identity, created-at, idle time, child command,
  size, acs version.
- `acs _proxy --list` enumerates `<dir>/*.sock`, queries each, reports and
  removes stale sockets; no `ps` parsing.
- Client prints an aligned table; `no sessions` when empty.

Tests: listing with attached, detached and stale sessions; output format.
close_reason: list.rs: side call to _proxy --list, STATUS_REPLY frames rendered as NAME/STATE/WHO/IDLE/AGE/COMMAND table, 'no sessions', not-installed case; tests: unit table + integration with attached, detached and stale socket

title: Client terminal: raw mode, guaranteed restore, signals
description:
Local tty handling (DESIGN §7).

- Raw mode with dtach's termios flags; the original termios restored on
  every exit path: normal return, SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT, and panic (drop
  guard plus signal handler, `panic = "abort"`).
- Self-pipe for signals; SIGWINCH surfaced as a resize event.
- Single-threaded `poll` loop skeleton with timers (escape timeout, pings).

Tests: termios flag computation as a unit test; a pty-based test that the
terminal is restored after the client is killed by a signal and after a
panic.

title: Integration test harness: local transport, pty runner, producers
description:
Shared test infrastructure for everything end-to-end (DESIGN §9.1).

- Temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` and temp `HOME` per test.
- Run the client under a pty with `--transport-cmd` pointing at the built
  binary's `_proxy` (no ssh).
- Deterministic producers (numbered lines, binary patterns incl. escape
  sequences) and a byte-exact capture of the client's stdout.
- A framed test client for driving the master/proxy directly.
- Transport killer to simulate a network drop mid-stream.

Acceptance: a smoke test attaches, runs a producer, and asserts byte
equality of output; harness usable from `cargo test`.

title: Client: ssh transport, handshake and byte-exact session
description:
The client's session path without reconnect (DESIGN §3, §4.4, §5, §6, §7).

- Spawn ssh via the builder; sync on `ACS-READY` (discard noise, show it
  under `-v`); detect `ACS-NEED` and hand off to install.
- HELLO with TERM, COLORTERM, size; DATA written verbatim to stdout while
  tracking the last offset; stdin through the command-key detector into
  INPUT with seq; RESIZE on SIGWINCH.
- `d`: DETACH, restore terminal (with observer resets), print
  `acs: detached from <host>/<name> - reattach with: acs <host> <name>`,
  exit 0. `x`: KILL, wait for EXIT, exit with the child's status.
- On creating a session print `acs: new session '<name>' on <host>` on
  stderr before raw mode.
- Exit codes per DESIGN §7.

Tests (harness): attach-or-create, byte-exact output incl. escape sequences,
detach and re-attach, `x` ends the remote session, EXIT status propagated,
new-session message.

title: Client: liveness, automatic reconnect and lossless resume
description:
Resume after network drops (DESIGN §5.2-5.4).

- PING after 3 s of silence; link dead after 10 s without a frame: kill ssh
  and redial with backoff 1 s -> 30 s, reset after a connection that lasted
  30 s. `--no-reconnect` disables.
- HELLO with resume{instance, offset}; handle resumed / gap (clear + redraw)
  / fresh ("session was restarted").
- Resend unacked input; drop keys typed while the link is known down, but
  keep command mode working (`d` detaches while down; `x` reports it needs
  the link).
- Status while disconnected: nothing for < 10 s; then one bottom-row line
  with save/restore cursor and the xterm title stack; one forced redraw
  after a resume that followed a status line.
- Cooked mode while ssh authenticates on redial (password / key touch).
- TAKEOVER ends the client with a message and the reattach hint.

Tests (harness): kill the transport mid-stream and assert the client's
stdout equals the producer's output byte for byte; input sent before the
drop is not duplicated; ring overflow while disconnected yields gap
handling; `--no-reconnect` exits on drop.
close_reason: reconnect.rs: Liveness (PING after 3s, dead after 10s), Backoff 1s->30s with reset, redial with resume, unacked resend, keys dropped while down but d works and x explains, status line + title stack, redraw via resize pair; 7 pty tests (cut, freeze, input once, --no-reconnect, detach while down, x needs link, gap) + unit tests; daemons close inherited fds

title: Client: immediate redial on network change
description:
Stretch goal from DESIGN §5.3: skip the backoff wait when the default route
changes (Wi-Fi switch, wake from sleep) — route socket / SCNetworkReachability
on macOS, netlink on Linux — where it is cheap to observe.

Tests: the reconnect scheduler redials immediately on an injected
"network changed" event.
close_reason: netwatch.rs: PF_ROUTE (address/interface messages only, ARP churn ignored) on macOS, NETLINK_ROUTE link/addr groups on Linux, FIFO injection for tests; offline wait redials at once on a change (max once per 2s) and resets backoff; unit tests + integration test (20s backoff bypassed)

title: Shared accounts: client identity and confirmed takeover
description:
Accident protection when several people use one remote account (DESIGN §4.5).

- Client identity `<local user>@<local hostname>`, overridable with
  `ACS_IDENTITY`, sent in HELLO; the master records attached and creator
  identities.
- Cross-identity attach gets BUSY{identity, since}; the client asks
  `take over? [y/N]` on the terminal, retries HELLO with `force` on yes;
  without a terminal it fails; `--force` skips the question.
- Same identity takes over silently (own dropped connection, own second
  terminal).

Tests (harness): same identity silent; different identity BUSY; force
takes over; non-tty without `--force` fails.
close_reason: Client identity (ACS_IDENTITY or user@host) in HELLO; BUSY answered with a cooked-mode [y/N] prompt naming who and since when, --force skips, non-tty declines; same identity silent takeover; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 5 pty tests

title: Multi-user integration tests in a Linux container
description:
Prove isolation between Unix accounts (DESIGN §4.5, §9.1) in a Linux
container with two users (docker/podman; the macOS host cannot switch uids
without root).

- Another user's pre-created `/tmp/acs-<uid>` (squatted, and symlinked) is
  refused.
- A connection from another uid to a master's socket is dropped.
- Two users' `main` sessions are independent.
- The whole `cargo test` suite also runs on Linux musl in the container.

Acceptance: one script (`scripts/test_linux.sh`) runs it end to end.
close_reason: tests/multiuser.rs (squatted dir, symlinked dir, foreign peer uid dropped by master, independent per-user main) + scripts/test_linux.sh running the full suite on Linux musl and the multi-user tests as root with alice/bob; all pass. The Linux run found and fixed a master backpressure stall and a replaced-binary spawn failure.

title: Frame codec, message types and ACS-READY marker
description:
Implement the wire protocol of DESIGN §5.1 in `proto.rs`.

- Frame: `type u8 | len u32 BE | payload`. Hard maximum frame length
  (e.g. 1 MiB) rejected as a protocol error.
- Incremental decoder that accepts arbitrary read boundaries.
- All message types: HELLO (incl. client identity, `force`, TERM, COLORTERM,
  size, optional resume{instance, offset}), WELCOME (resumed/gap/fresh,

title: Run the session menu and the attach over one ssh connection
description:
Wanted: a plain `acs <host>` makes two ssh connections, one to list sessions for the menu and one for the session, each paying a full TCP + key exchange + auth handshake. Reduce it to a single call to connect faster. The user's `acs -v corello` on v0.6.0 shows `ssh … _proxy --list` followed by `ssh -o ControlMaster=no -o ControlPath=none … _proxy --session main --mode attach-or-create`.

Verified (v0.6.0): src/pick.rs `choose` lists with `list::query(.., Call::Side, ..)`, then the attach dials its own connection. The session call opts out of multiplexing on purpose (DESIGN §3: a reconnect must never wait on a dead multiplexer), so even `ControlMaster auto` + `ControlPersist` cannot share it. Ending a session with 'x' in the menu is a third kind of call, `_proxy --kill <name>` (pick.rs `end`, src/proxy.rs). The second handshake costs a few hundred ms, more through a jump host, and a hardware key needs two touches.

This revisits a recorded decision: DESIGN §4.4 says "reusing one connection for both is not worth a second proxy mode." The implementing PR updates §4.4 (and §3/§4.3/§5.1 as needed) and says why the decision changed: connect latency and the double auth.

Sketch: a picker mode on the session connection, e.g. `_proxy --pick` with the usual transport options. The proxy first sends the session list as frames (the STATUS data `--list` gathers). The client decides on that list exactly as today (none detached: create; else the menu in menu.rs, unchanged). Menu actions travel on the same connection: '.' (refresh with attached sessions), 'x' (end a session, then a fresh list), new. The pick ends with the ordinary HELLO naming the session and mode (and `force` after a confirmed takeover); the proxy then connects to or starts that master and relays as now. Leaving the menu (Esc/exit) closes the connection cleanly.

Unchanged: redials (they know the session and use the plain session call), `acs <host> <name>`, `--new`, `--list`, and the non-tty fallback, which are already a single call. Keep the install path working: a host without acs answers ACS-NEED on the pick call as on any other, so install, then continue. The ACS-READY marker and the dial deadlines (§5.3) apply to the pick phase. Mind the menu's idle time: the connection sits open while the user reads it, with no liveness pings before WELCOME.

Done when `acs -v <host>` with detached sessions shows one ssh invocation from list to attach, 'x' and '.' work without extra ssh calls, the proto/proxy changes have unit tests and an end-to-end test (scripts/e2e_ssh.sh or the in-process tests) covers pick → attach on one connection, and DESIGN/README describe it.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #40 (1dc2233): _proxy --pick runs the session menu, x and the attach over one ssh connection

title: Specify an ssh local port forward on the command line, mirroring ssh -L
description:
User's words: "Make it possible that ssh port forward can be specified on command line, mirroring ssh '-L'".

Today `-L` is rejected outright: the accepted ssh options are exactly `-i -p -J -F -o` (src/cli.rs:162), and any other short option falls through to src/cli.rs:192 and errors with `unknown option -L`.

## It is already possible, badly

`-o` is an unvalidated pass-through — acs never inspects the value — so this works right now:

```sh
acs -o LocalForward="8080 localhost:80" box
```

That matters for scoping: this bead is **not** about making forwarding possible, it is about making it correct and ergonomic. Three reasons it still deserves doing, in order of weight:

**1. The `-o` route is actually wrong, not merely ugly.** `user_opts` is shared by all three `Call` kinds (src/ssh.rs:96-123). `Call::Session` is the user's shell, but `Call::Side` (`acs list <host>`, remote install, the session menu) and `Call::Batch` (`acs list` over every alias, §7.3) build their argv from the same `user_opts`. A `LocalForward` given via `-o` is therefore handed to every one of those ssh processes as well, so several concurrent ssh children try to bind the same local port. ssh's default `ExitOnForwardFailure=no` means each one warns and carries on, so it is noisy and wrong rather than fatal. A real `-L` can be emitted for `Call::Session` only.

**2. No validation.** A malformed `-o LocalForward=` spec is discovered by ssh, per dial, mid-reconnect-loop, as a line of ssh stderr on a terminal acs is otherwise keeping clean.

**3. Ergonomics and muscle memory.** acs replaces `ssh`+`dtach`; `-L` is the spelling people already know, and `-o LocalForward="8080 localhost:80"` requires knowing that the config-file form uses a space where `-L` uses a colon.

## Verified about the code (v0.11.4)

- **The argv is built in exactly one place**, `Transport::argv()` at src/ssh.rs:96-123, layout `<ssh> <fixed opts for the Call> <user_opts…> [-i <key>] -- <destination> <remote command>`. Every call site funnels through it (src/client.rs:357, src/install.rs:210, src/list.rs:61,142, src/pick.rs:54,463).
- **Order is load-bearing.** ssh keeps the *first* value it sees, which is why acs puts its own transport options before the user's (docs/DESIGN.md:876-883). A forward must be emitted with or after `user_opts`, not before.
- **Reconnect needs no work.** `reconnect::run()` (src/reconnect.rs:60-169) clones `ClientArgs` once at :75 and re-dials through the same builder each pass (:76-88 → client.rs:357), so the argv is rebuilt from scratch every dial. A forward stored on `Transport` is re-applied on every reconnect for free.
- **But the forward does drop during a redial.** The old ssh child is dead, so the listening socket is released and rebound. Worth one line in the docs, and it is the argument for `-o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes` being considered — a rebind that loses a race (a stale TIME_WAIT, a second acs on the same port) otherwise leaves a live session with a silently dead forward.
- **No duplicate bead.** Every "forward" hit in src/ is keystroke forwarding (src/keys.rs:62, src/proxy.rs:287); `acs-aps` is ssh *agent* forwarding, a different thing. A grep for LocalForward/tunnel/socks over src/, docs/, README.md and tests/ finds nothing, and all 107 records in .beads/issues.jsonl were checked.

## Implementation sketch

1. src/cli.rs:162 — accept `Short('L')`, repeatable, and validate the `[bind:]port:host:hostport` spec with a real error. USAGE at src/cli.rs:20-51 needs the entry too.
2. src/ssh.rs:51-66 — a new `Transport` field (`local_forwards: Vec<String>`) rather than stuffing `user_opts`, precisely so it can be gated.
3. src/ssh.rs:96-123 — emit `-L <spec>` after `user_opts`, **only when `call == Call::Session`**.
4. Optional, and the reason to look at acs-c9d: a `local_forwards` list setting, global and per alias, mirroring `local_networks` exactly (Config field config.rs:129, `Option` field on Alias config.rs:99, `KEYS` :166, `ALIAS_KEYS` :199, a type const beside `NETWORKS` :211, a `*_for(alias)` accessor like :509, and a branch in config_cmd::typed at config_cmd.rs:93). Per-alias is the natural home for "this host always needs its database forwarded". `acs-mbd` (identity file per alias) is the precedent for a per-alias ssh-affecting setting.
5. Docs: docs/DESIGN.md §3 (:133-152) and §7.1 (:840-883), README.md:173-182.

## Scope decisions to make when taking this

- **`-R` and `-D` as well, or `-L` only?** The user asked for `-L`. `-R` and `-D` are the same plumbing and the same gating; doing all three at once costs little more than one. Decide explicitly rather than by omission.
- **Runtime add/remove is out of scope.** Command mode (docs/DESIGN.md:694-745, dispatch at src/keys.rs:487) could plausibly grow a key, but there is no channel to reconfigure a *running* ssh: acs disables ssh's `~C` escape with `-e none` (src/ssh.rs:10) and disables the control socket (`ControlMaster=no`, `ControlPath=none`). Changing a forward would mean tearing the link down and redialling. Command mode also has no prompt or line editor, so there is nowhere to type `8080:localhost:80`. Note it as a non-goal.
- **Does `-L` suppress the `-o LocalForward` path?** No reason to; `-o` stays the unvalidated escape hatch. But the Session-only gating means the two behave differently, which the docs should say out loud.

Done when `acs -L 8080:localhost:80 box` forwards the port, the flag is repeatable, a bad spec is a clear acs error before any ssh is spawned, the forward is passed to the session ssh but **not** to the `Call::Side` and `Call::Batch` calls, it survives a reconnect, unit tests cover the argv for all three `Call` kinds plus spec parsing good and bad, and DESIGN §7.1 and the README document it along with the brief drop across a redial.

title: Resolve user@host through the host's configured entries, as that user

title: Create temp files with O_EXCL and full randomness instead of the process id
description:
Security, symlink and predictable-name attacks. Several temp paths are predictable and opened in a way that follows symlinks: upgrade.rs uses .acs-upgrade.<getpid()> with File::create (O_TRUNC, follows links) and 32-bit randomness elsewhere, update_check.rs uses .update-check.<getpid()>, scripts/install.sh uses "$2.new.$$" with cp and ln -s, and xtask/src/bump.rs uses /tmp/acs-release-<pid>-<version>.

This matters because both the upgrade and the installer tell the user to re-run under sudo into /usr/local/bin and /usr/local/lib/acs, which on Intel Homebrew and hand-managed hosts are routinely group- or user-writable. Pre-creating the predictable name as a symlink turns the root-run create or cp into an arbitrary-file overwrite, then chmod 755.

Also worth narrowing while here: upgrade::link_candidates adds <dir>/acs for every directory on PATH and relink writes into any that currently points at the running exe.

Done when every temp file is created O_EXCL with full-width randomness (never the pid), the installer uses install -m 755 rather than cp plus chmod, and a test or at least a comment records why.

title: Decode frames just read before judging liveness, so a stdout stall is not a dead link
description:
The client loop (src/client.rs:959-972) reads the link into dec and immediately calls liveness.tick(), but liveness.heard() is only updated in the decode loop at the top of the next iteration (client.rs:734), so heard reflects the previous iteration. Normally microseconds, but write_output -> sys::write_all(STDOUT) (client.rs:657-674) blocks for as long as the terminal is not reading (emulator stalled, flow control). After a stall over 10 s the next poll returns at once, the new frames are read, and tick sees now >= heard + dead_after, so lost(link): a needless ssh kill, redial, status line and Ctrl-L although PONGs were sitting in the pipe.

Done when the client decodes after the read before ticking (or treats a readable link as heard), with a test that delays stdout consumption past the liveness deadline and asserts no redial.
